name: One-Take Oner
summary: The whole film as one unbroken camera move through a UI set: dashboard corridor, reveal room, crane down to the anomaly, pull out the window.
look: A light architectural CSS-3D set whose walls are tiled with dashboards, lit by a teal doorway at the vanishing point. Frame guides, a take slate and a floor-plan mini-map with a coral camera path sit on top of every frame.

components.name: UI corridor set
components.role: CSS 3D box tunnel whose walls are tiled with product dashboards; the “world” the camera travels through

components.name: Doorway / light portal
components.role: teal glow at the vanishing point that pulls the eye and becomes the reveal room

components.name: Foreground wipe pillar
components.role: dark blurred edge that crosses the lens to hide a stitch between two long takes

components.name: Tilted watch panel
components.role: live metric rows on a table surface the camera cranes down onto

components.name: Anomaly card
components.role: the one flat, frontal object in a 3D world — the proof moment and the human’s decision

components.name: Plan mini-map + slate
components.role: floor plan with a coral camera path, take number and timecode; makes the move legible in stills

motion.name: Continuous dolly
motion.how: camera z moves at constant speed (linear ease) through the hook, one tile row passes per beat at 120 BPM (0.5 s); never stops, only changes direction on bar lines

motion.name: Hidden stitch wipe
motion.how: foreground pillar crosses the frame in 0.25 s (power2.in), cut happens at 50% opacity black, lands exactly on the drop at 0:08

motion.name: Crane + settle
motion.how: vertical move 1.2 s power3.inOut over 2 bars, panel rotateX 38° → 0° in the last 0.5 s; card lifts z +80 px on the downbeat with back.out(1.4)

story: Hook: dolly down a corridor of 38 dashboards. Reveal: a foreground pillar wipes and we are in the teal Acme Pulse room on the drop. Proof: crane down onto the watch panel, the coral row lifts into “Checkout conversion −18%” and the cursor hits Roll back. CTA: pull back out the window to the lockup, “You ship. Pulse watches.” and Start free.
adapt: Replace the dashboard tiles on the corridor walls with screenshots of the tools your customers juggle today, and make the reveal room your product’s main screen. The crane-down target is whatever single object carries your value (a PR check, an invoice, a ticket).

references.note: how 1917 hid stitches behind foreground elements and darkness
long take definition; Rope (1948) as the classic example
Apple’s one-take Hermitage film as a brand-scale oner

fit.risk: A oner lives or dies on pacing; if the camera drifts between beats the viewer loses the story, and 3D sets are the most expensive thing in this kit.
